contexts.name: Analysis History Ledger

contexts.name: Analyze File Intake & Upload Constraints
contexts.description: Drag/drop and file-picker intake for CVs: the drop zone, file-list UI, drop routing between candidate slots, file-accept/size validation and the global drag listener.

contexts.name: Analyze Form Fields & JD Library
contexts.description: The Analyze tab's form surface: collapsible layout, footer/optional columns, paste-JD row and the saved-JD picker backed by the JD library hook.

contexts.name: Analysis Result Panels - Job-Fit, Interview & Compare
contexts.description: The job-fit skill-gap view, interview kit with soft-signal detection, and the side-by-side candidate comparison tab, sharing common result-panel primitives.

contexts.name: Match Reasoning & Explanations
contexts.description: Generate and cache the LLM-backed explanation behind a match score: the reasoning cache key/policy, its run, the API route and the panel that surfaces it on a match card.

contexts.name: Match Results & Comparison
contexts.description: Present ranked match results: cards, skill chips, bulk actions, group-eval banner and the side-by-side job compare view. Consumes the match run's output and renders it for the Match tab.

contexts.name: Match Run & Weights
contexts.description: Run a candidate-against-jobs match: the Match tab, per-job weight controls, and the deterministic scoring input/resolution behind the /api/match endpoint.

contexts.name: Candidate Roster & Matrix
contexts.description: List, filter and drill into saved candidate profiles: the roster table, the archetype-by-skill candidate matrix, and the Profile tab shell (rebuild warnings, completeness, deep links).

contexts.name: Candidate Archetypes & Role Taxonomy
contexts.description: Manage the reusable archetype library (role templates that seed and validate a CandidateProfile) and the role-family taxonomy behind it. Backs the Archetype Manager CRUD panel and its API routes.

contexts.name: GitHub Evidence & CV Utilities
contexts.description: Pull GitHub repo evidence into a candidate analysis and auto-fill / vary CV-derived profile fields. Backs the GitHub analysis panel and CV provenance helpers.

contexts.name: Candidate Profile Editing
contexts.description: Build and persist a structured CandidateProfile: the editor form, AI-assisted draft fill, field/evidence layout and its submit/payload plumbing. Backs the Profile tab's edit surface and the /api/profile endpoints.

contexts.name: Analysis Result Panels - Extraction, Salary & Actions
contexts.description: The result-panel shell plus its extraction and salary tabs: progress/scan chrome, archetype banner, quality strip, disposition editing and add-to-pipeline actions.

contexts.name: Analyze Run & Streaming Progress
contexts.description: Kick off and stream a full AI analysis run: the workspace shell, tab, API client, run policy/pipeline-ref plumbing and the underlying /api/analyze and /api/extract-text endpoints.

contexts.name: JD Linting, Revisions & Public Detail Page
contexts.description: Enforce JD quality limits and lint rules, track JD revision history, retry stalled analyses, and render the public-facing JD detail page (body + apply actions) that candidates see.
contexts.businessFeature: JD Linting, Revisions & Public Detail Page

contexts.name: JD Template Manager
contexts.description: Manage reusable JD templates: list, edit and render templates that seed the JD builder. Includes the template CRUD API and the shared template-rendering helper used by both the library and public JD pages.

contexts.name: JD Builder, Generation & Editing
contexts.description: Author a JD from scratch or AI-generate one: the builder wizard with its checklist and fields, the generate panel, the modal editor used to make and stage edits, and the save/ingest-job persistence path.

contexts.name: Job Posting Modal & Candidate Cohort Views
contexts.description: The job posting detail modal: shared posting fields/types, markdown rendering of the JD body, cohort comparison across postings, and the AI coach's apply/salary suggestions surfaced inside the modal.
contexts.businessFeature: Job Posting Modal & Candidate Cohort Views

contexts.name: Job Posting Authoring & Ad Ingestion
contexts.description: Ingest a raw job ad (paste/upload), split it into candidate draft postings, and manage the drafts launchpad before a job goes live. Covers the ad-ingest panel, its results view, and the ingest API/lib.

contexts.name: Candidate Rediscovery & Alerts
contexts.description: Rediscover past applicants who match a new or reopened job: relevance scoring, rematch source tracking, an alert feed for recruiters, and the panel/feed UI to review and act on rediscovered candidates.

contexts.name: Sourcing Campaigns & Outreach
contexts.description: Run outreach campaigns against a job's candidate pool: pick a campaign variant, send outreach messages, and track campaign performance. Backed by the recruiter-run pipeline and the campaign persistence layer.

contexts.name: Recruiter Candidate Pool & Coaching
contexts.description: Recruiter-facing candidate pool for a job: view matched candidates by column/stage, apply fairness checks, and use the AI coach panel to loosen filters or edit stage criteria. Also covers salary-band computation used to qualify candidates and the winnability signal shown to recruiters.

contexts.name: Job Lifecycle, Listing & Publishing
contexts.description: The Jobs tab table and its lifecycle: list/filter open roles, publish, close, and merge status changes. Owns the jobs DB access layer, the lifecycle status strip, deep-linkable filters, and the request-guard/list hook backing the table.

contexts.name: JD Saved Ledger & Library Tab
contexts.description: The Library tab shell and its saved-JD ledger: table/row/filter UI for all saved JDs, per-JD detail rail/modal with coach trace and candidate list, and the ledger's artifact and navigation logic. This is the landing surface a recruiter sees when opening the JD library.

contexts.name: Interview Scheduler & Self-Scheduling
contexts.description: The interview-scheduling panel reachable from a candidate's drawer: SchedulerControl.tsx/SchedulerToolbar.tsx are the entry point, SchedulerRemindersRow.tsx/SchedulerRunHistory.tsx/SchedulerSummaryBadges.tsx show reminder and run-history state, and useSchedulerControlState.ts owns it. PipelineSelfSchedulingPanel.tsx lets the candidate pick their own slot and PipelineVoiceScreenPanel.tsx launches the AI voice-screen step, both driven off the same scheduler state.

contexts.name: Pipeline Bulk Actions & Command
contexts.description: Moving and bulk-deciding candidates: pipeline-command.ts is the single command dispatcher behind POST /api/pipeline/command, db/pipeline.ts is its data layer, and pipeline-status.ts computes the resulting stage/status. PipelineBulkActionBar.tsx/PipelineBulkDecideRow.tsx/PipelineBulkOutreachButton.tsx/pipelineBulkConfirm.ts drive multi-select bulk actions, PipelineMoveStageControl.tsx/pipelineMoveTargets.ts drive single-candidate stage moves, and PassPreviewModal.tsx/PipelineAiActionsGrid.tsx/PipelineSlaEditor.tsx are the related AI-action and SLA controls that issue commands through the same dispatcher.

contexts.name: Candidate Result, Evidence & Signals
contexts.description: Inside the candidate drawer, the panels that show why a candidate scored the way they did: PipelineCandidateResultView.tsx/PipelineCandidateRow.tsx/PipelineCandidateNoteField.tsx render the result and note-taking, PipelineGithubEvidenceCard.tsx/PipelineHumanScorecardCard.tsx/PipelineInterviewOutcomeCard.tsx/PipelineInterviewTelemetryStrip.tsx surface GitHub, human-scorecard and interview evidence, and PipelineSalaryBenchmarkHint.tsx/PipelineRematchAffordance.tsx/PipelineCommsList.tsx/PipelineTokenLink.tsx round out the signal panels. pipeline-fairness/github-handle/screening test files validate these signals.

contexts.name: Pipeline Candidate Drawer Core
contexts.description: The candidate drawer shell that opens from a board row: PipelineCandidateDrawer.tsx is the entry point, PipelineDrawerHeader.tsx/PipelineDrawerFooterLinks.tsx frame it, and PipelineDrawerHistoryList.tsx/PipelineTimelineItemRow.tsx render the candidate's full timeline sourced from candidate-timeline.ts via GET /api/pipeline/[id]/timeline. usePipelineCandidateDrawerState.ts owns the drawer's open/tab state.

contexts.name: Pipeline Tab Shell & Live Updates
contexts.description: The Pipeline tab's outer shell and its live-update wiring: PipelineTab.tsx is the entry point, PipelineStatHeader.tsx/PipelineTodayRail.tsx/CommandBar.tsx render the top-of-tab chrome, and pipeline-events-public.ts plus GET /api/pipeline/events stream stage-change SSE events that PipelineActivityFeed.tsx and PipelineDegradedIntakeBanner.tsx react to. pipelineEventCatalog.ts/pipelineTranslator.ts/pipelineRenderDiet.ts are the shared event-naming, i18n and render-throttling helpers used across the whole Pipeline board.

contexts.name: Application Status Tracking
contexts.description: Lets a candidate check on their own application after submitting: application-status.ts/application-status-store.ts compute and persist the status shown at /status/[token] via GET /api/status/[token], and completeness-followup.ts sends a nudge when required fields are still missing. Separate from the apply flows themselves because this is a post-submission, read-mostly surface.

contexts.name: Quick Apply Form
contexts.description: A one-field, low-friction alternative to the conversational flow at /apply/[id]/quick: QuickApplyForm.tsx is the entry point, backed by POST /api/apply/[id]/quick. Kept separate from Conversational Apply because it is a distinct, self-contained candidate-facing surface with its own route and no shared UI.

contexts.name: Decision Rules & Analysis Summary
contexts.description: Configures the screening rules that drive automated decisions and shows the plain-language summary of an analysis: decision-config-schema.ts validates the rule config, decision-config-store.ts persists it via GET/POST /api/decisions/config, and decisionsFloorDisclosure.ts computes the minimum-score floor disclosure. DecisionsRulesModal.tsx is where rules are edited; DecisionsAnalysisSummaryModal.tsx/Body.tsx plus decisionsAnalysisSummaryData.ts render the human-readable explanation of why a candidate scored the way they did.

contexts.name: Reconsider Queue & Decision Records
contexts.description: Persists the auditable, hash-chained decision record and lets a recruiter reconsider a prior verdict: decision-record-store.ts writes records, decision-hash.ts chains each record to the previous one for tamper-evidence, and POST /api/decisions/reconsider plus GET /api/decisions/records expose the flow. DecisionsReconsiderQueue.tsx/DecisionsRoleRow.tsx render the queue of candidates awaiting reconsideration, with decisionsSelectionHygiene.ts guarding against selecting an already-decided candidate.

contexts.name: Screen Wave Decisions
contexts.description: The bulk 'screen wave' flow that runs a screening pass over an entire cohort at once: screen-wave.ts computes the wave and screen-wave-approval.ts gates approval, exposed via POST /api/decisions/screen-wave. DecisionsScreenWaveModal/ConfirmModal/Lists render the wave-selection and confirmation UI, decisionsScreenWaveTypes.ts defines its shape, and useDecisionsScreenWave.ts holds the modal's state.

contexts.name: Decisions AI Review & Compliance
contexts.description: Runs and displays the AI-assisted screening verdict for a role: DecisionsAiReviewCard.tsx/DecisionsAiReviewCardBody.tsx/DecisionsAiReviewsSection.tsx render per-candidate AI review cards backed by decisionsAiReviewCardLogic.ts and decision-attribution.ts (which attributes a verdict to the model/prompt version that produced it). DecisionsComplianceSection.tsx/DecisionsComplianceImpactCheck.tsx and compliance-regimes.ts surface which legal regime (e.g. AI Act) applies and its impact, backed by GET /api/compliance.

contexts.name: Group Eval Differentiators & Sanity Checks
contexts.description: Pure scoring/analysis helpers that feed the Group Eval verdict: group-eval-differentiators.ts extracts the standout traits that separate candidates in a shortlist, and sanity-checks.ts runs guardrail checks over a group-eval result before it's shown, each with its own unit test. Kept separate from the UI contexts because these are pure functions with no rendering concerns.

contexts.name: Group Eval Comparison Table
contexts.description: Renders the side-by-side candidate comparison grid inside the Group Eval modal: GroupEvalComparisonTable.tsx lays out the grid, GroupEvalComparisonCells.tsx/GroupEvalComparisonRows.tsx render individual cells and rows, GroupEvalSalaryCell.tsx and groupEvalSalaryScale.ts handle the salary-band column specifically, and GroupEvalPrimitives.tsx/groupEvalHelpers.ts are the shared atoms and formatting helpers reused across the table.

contexts.name: Channel Receivers & Setup
contexts.description: Onboards a new intake channel: the ad-forms pane, add-receiver modal and receiver table manage the list of configured receivers (useChannelsReceivers.ts backs them), while the setup guide, email-intake wizard and CV-sim card walk a recruiter through configuring an email relay and previewing what an inbound CV submission will look like. Distinct from the tab shell because these components own their own modal/wizard flows and receiver CRUD.

contexts.name: Channels Tab Shell & Filters
contexts.description: The Channels tab's own container: ChannelsTab.tsx composes the stage switcher, filter menu and empty states, channelsSections.ts/channelsAccent.ts drive the per-channel styling and layout, and useChannelsData.ts loads the tab's aggregate data. This is the shell a developer opens to change tab navigation, filtering, or the empty-state copy, as opposed to any one channel's setup flow.

contexts.name: Inbound Channel Webhooks
contexts.description: Receives inbound applications and provider webhooks: db/channels.ts models the channel/receiver tables, webhook-idempotency.ts guards replayed webhook deliveries, and the three /api/channels routes handle a tokenized inbound submission and inbound/outbound webhook callbacks. This is the ingestion boundary that feeds the pipeline before the Channels tab ever renders anything.

contexts.name: Comms Status, Resend & Delivery UI
contexts.description: Tracks and surfaces the delivery lifecycle of a sent communication: comms-status.ts computes bounced/delivered/opened state, the resend and provider-callback API routes update it, and useDeliveryCapability.ts exposes whether the tenant's channel can actually deliver. The Channels-tab comms table/rows/message-modal/bounced-resend components are the UI that reads this status and lets a user resend or inspect a message.

contexts.name: ATS Integration & Egress
contexts.description: A vendor-neutral outbound integration that replaces a whole-DB dump: ats-record.ts purely maps a pipeline entry + job + latest sealed decision + offer into a stable versioned kp.ats.v1 record, and ats-egress.ts fetches those rows and POSTs signed lifecycle webhooks. Config (webhook URL, subscribed events, write-only signing secret) lives in the lazily-created ats_config table via ats-config-store.ts under a strict secret doctrine (getAtsConfig returns only hasSecret), and ats-webhook.ts defines the event types plus the HMAC-SHA256 'sha256=<hex>' signature. Delivery is best-effort with a 5s timeout; candidate.hired fires live from offer-finalize.ts on offer-accept, and IntegrationsCard configures it plus a test ping.

contexts.name: Comms Dispatch & Envelope Core
contexts.description: The core outbound-message pipeline: comms.ts orchestrates building and sending a candidate communication, comms-envelope.ts assembles the versioned message envelope, comms-dispatch.ts performs the actual send, and comms-locale.ts/comms-recipient.ts/comms-view.ts resolve locale, recipient and read-model concerns. comms-truth.ts is the single source of truth used across the comms feature, and POST /api/comms is the entry point that triggers a send.

contexts.name: Group Eval Verdict & Fairness
contexts.description: The Group Evaluation modal itself: GroupEvalModal.tsx is the entry point, group-eval.ts/group-eval-run.ts orchestrate the AI comparison run and group-eval-governance.ts enforces who may launch it, all persisted via POST /api/decisions/group-eval. GroupEvalAiVerdict, GroupEvalFairnessPanel, GroupEvalRisks, GroupEvalNotices and GroupEvalPerCandidateTabs render the verdict, fairness and risk panels, with GroupEvalLegacyView as the pre-redesign fallback and useGroupEval.ts holding the modal's state.

contexts.name: Decisions Tab Shell
contexts.description: The Decisions tab's outer container: DecisionsTab.tsx is the entry point, DecisionsHeader.tsx and DecisionsBanners.tsx render the top-of-tab chrome, DecisionsModals.tsx routes to whichever sub-modal is open, and DecisionsShared.tsx/decisionsTypes.ts hold cross-cutting types and small shared pieces used by every other Decisions sub-context. DecisionsEmptyShared/DecisionsEmptyHandoff cover the tab's empty states.

contexts.name: Conversational Apply Intake
contexts.description: The full conversational apply experience a candidate sees at /apply/[id]: ConversationalApply.tsx is the entry point, apply.ts/apply-intake.ts run the multi-turn intake logic, cv-intake.ts and lead-intake.ts/lead-payload.ts handle CV parsing and lead capture along the way, all persisted through GET/PATCH /api/apply/[id].

contexts.name: Pipeline Board Layout & Filters
contexts.description: The kanban board's own layout engine: PipelineBoard.tsx/PipelinePopulatedBoard.tsx render the stage columns via PipelineBoardStageCell.tsx, pipelineBoardGrid.ts/pipelineBoardLayout.ts compute the grid, and PipelineFilterBar.tsx/PipelineFacetRow.tsx/pipelineBoardFilters.ts drive filtering. PipelineSavedViews.tsx/PipelineViewDialog.tsx/pipelineViews.ts let a user save and switch between filtered views, all fetched via GET /api/pipeline.

contexts.name: Interview Scorecards, Rubric & Transcript Review
contexts.description: Score a completed interview against the rubric: human and AI scorecard sections/forms, the telemetry strip, and the transcript viewer for reviewing what was said. Backed by the interviews DB table, rubric/scorecard lib, and the scorecard API route.

contexts.name: Interview Prep Pack & Run of Show
contexts.description: Generate the AI interview-prep pack for an upcoming interview: prep questions/notes, a run-of-show agenda, and the grounded interview-brief scripts. Covers the prep modal, its header/load-states/notes/questions sub-views, and the prep API route.
contexts.businessFeature: Interview Prep Pack & Run of Show

contexts.name: Scheduling Calendar, Slots & Candidate Picker
contexts.description: The interview-slot calendar: week-view grid, add-to-calendar links, timezone conversion, meeting-link display, and the public token-based picker page a candidate uses to pick a slot.

contexts.name: Voice Provider Engines, Telemetry & Transcript
contexts.description: The voice-provider abstraction (OpenAI Realtime / ElevenLabs switcher): per-provider event handling, preflight checks, minute pricing, environment validation, session telemetry, transcript capture, and the ElevenLabs agent setup script.

contexts.name: Interview Simulation & Comparison
contexts.description: Simulate an interview round, attach simulated outcomes to a candidate, compare interviews, and produce interview recommendations (incl. student mode).

contexts.name: Voice Interview Session Lifecycle & UI
contexts.description: Create, connect, run and complete an in-browser voice interview session: the sidebar/session UI components, the interview-lab and interview-run orchestration, session-duration tracking, and the create/connect/complete/revoke/by-entry API routes plus the public interview pages.

contexts.name: Self-Scheduling Invites, Lifecycle & Reminders
contexts.description: Send self-scheduling invites (single/bulk), track each invite's lifecycle bucket (pending/attention/history) with recruiter controls, and drive reminder policy/delivery. Backed by the schedule store and the invite API routes; hosts the schedule tab shell and its interviewed/pending lists.

contexts.name: Scheduler & Automation CLI
contexts.description: The persistent scheduler that decides when to fire an automation pass, its store, the schedule API, app instrumentation hook-in, and the Python automation CLI/eval used to run and score automation offline.

contexts.name: Candidate Pre-boarding Questionnaire
contexts.description: The candidate-facing side of onboarding hand-off: the token-gated pre-boarding entry questionnaire reached from an accepted offer, and the library/route that reads/writes a candidate's intake answers.

contexts.name: Onboarding Run Detail, Checklist & Signatures
contexts.description: The single onboarding run's detail view: per-task checklist progress, audit ledgers, and the e-sign provider seam that stamps completed documents. Reads/writes the task-state and signature tables for one run.

contexts.name: Onboarding Templates & Run Management
contexts.description: The recruiter's onboarding template library and run list: creating a reusable checklist template per role, starting a run for a new hire, and the Onboarding tab's empty states and run list/summary UI.

contexts.name: Automation Passes, Fairness & ROI Gating
contexts.description: The decision logic run on each automation pass over the pipeline: fairness checks, ROI gating, cache-key derivation so repeat passes are idempotent, and the approval-kind taxonomy that labels what a pass proposes.

contexts.name: Offers & Onboarding
contexts.description: Generate, send, and finalize candidate offers via a tokenized public offer page, gated by offer policy.

contexts.name: Dev Tab Shell & Cases Table
contexts.description: The Dev tab's outer shell: the tab switcher between Cases/Define views, the cases table with its empty/empty-ledger states, shared dev-tab types and helpers, and the data-fetch hook feeding the table. Composes the need-analysis and publishing/detail sub-contexts underneath it.

contexts.name: Dev Case Publishing & Detail View
contexts.description: Publishing a designed dev case and reviewing it as a posting: the case-detail view (header, channels, shortlist, internal notes), the apply-token pill, publish/seed helpers, postings/publish API routes and the lifecycle-review panel shown alongside it.

contexts.name: Dev Submission Review & Evaluation
contexts.description: Recruiter-side review of a candidate's dev case submission: the eval panel (scores, process trace), authenticity/code-review-status checks, provenance strip, side-by-side submission comparison, and the submission row/form list UI.

contexts.name: Dev Skill-Profile, Outcomes & Outbox
contexts.description: What happens after a dev case closes: the verifiable skill-profile (lib, DB, verify token API, public page), hire/no-hire outcome tracking and promotion into an offer, and the comms outbox that shows what was sent to the candidate.

contexts.name: Dev Cohort, Probe & Interview Kit
contexts.description: Post-case signal for recruiters: cohort probe-strength analysis and its banner/panel UI, feedback capture, and the generated interview kit used to prep a human follow-up interview.

contexts.name: Dev Case Evaluation & Lifecycle (Python)
contexts.description: The Python side of judging and closing the loop on a dev case: submission evaluation, LLM-judge scoring, lifecycle audits/eval, interview-scenario generation, reflection and provenance/event processing. Consumed by the TS evaluation and lifecycle routes.

contexts.name: Dev Case Design & Authoring (Python)
contexts.description: The Python engine that turns a role need into a runnable dev case: need analysis, case design/calibration, real-corpus sourcing, scenario/seed generation and the CLI entry point. Backs the TS case-authoring routes; evaluation and lifecycle logic now live in a sibling context.

contexts.name: Dev Lifecycle Management
contexts.description: Approve/close/redesign flow for dev cases: the lifecycle row/section UI, the SLA and seed-diff checks behind it, and the /api/devcase/lifecycle routes plus core devcase DB access. Cohort/probe and skill-profile/outcomes now live in sibling contexts.

contexts.name: Dev Live Work Surface & Session
contexts.description: The candidate-facing dev case workspace: the apply-token live coding surface and form, the session API that tracks and submits it, and the repo activity/snapshot libs that back authenticity checks. Recruiter-side submission review and scoring now live in a sibling context.

contexts.name: Dev Case Need Analysis & Orchestration
contexts.description: The start of a dev case: capturing the role need, running the analyze/design/reflection orchestration (backed by devcase-orchestrator/run/constraints and dev-control), and the /api/devcase root+control+source routes. Publishing/detail and the tab shell now live in sibling contexts.

contexts.name: Salary, Recruiter & Winnability Scoring
contexts.description: Downstream scoring built on the matching core: ATS pass-through, campaign and group-compare orchestration, insights generation, jobs data access, live-case scoring, match-reasoning prep, recruiter scoring, salary bands and winnability.

contexts.name: Salary/Campaign CLIs & Script Wrappers
contexts.description: CLI entry points for campaign, group-compare, jobs ingestion and market salary lookup, plus the thin scripts/ wrappers that expose the pipeline to shell/CI use.

contexts.name: Seed Data & Fixtures
contexts.description: Deterministic seed datasets and generators for jobs (Česká spořitelna), candidates, pipeline stages, analyses and salary benchmarks, plus the CV-fixture rendering script used by the eval harness.

contexts.name: Pipeline Test Suite - Devcase & Live Case
contexts.description: Pytest coverage for the dev-case module: case analysis/design/lifecycle/evaluate/models/provenance/reflect/source flows, its CLI, and the live-case runner.

contexts.name: Pipeline Test Suite - Salary, Profile & Recruiter
contexts.description: Pytest coverage for salary bands/sanity, candidate profiling and its CLI/draft flow, recruiter scoring, jobs ingestion, group-compare and the matrix CLI.

contexts.name: Pipeline Test Suite - Scoring & Matching
contexts.description: Pytest coverage for the deterministic scoring core: matching, match-reasoning, scoring/score-sanity contracts, archetype sanity, taxonomy contracts/graph, transferability/transform, weight proposals, winnability, the registry and insights.

contexts.name: Pipeline Test Suite - Extraction & Parsing
contexts.description: Pytest coverage for CV/JD extraction and parsing correctness: Gemini truncation handling, PDF parsing quality, redaction, i18n/locale of prompts, embeddings and early-career/authenticity/soft-signal detection.

contexts.name: Pipeline Test Suite - Automation & Evaluation Harness
contexts.description: Shared pytest infra (helpers, gated-run entry point) plus coverage for automation/campaign flows, the Claude CLI bridge, interview rubrics/scenarios, fairness, pipeline degrade/diagram contracts, process events and seed-data generation.

contexts.name: Evaluation Harness (Matching & Interview)
contexts.description: The offline evaluation CLI and its runner: matching/interview eval and optimize, threshold definitions, ElevenLabs voice backend and shared report styling.

contexts.name: Core Pipeline CLIs
contexts.description: The primary CLI entry points the Next.js API shells out to for extraction, matching, profiling, reasoning, recruiter scoring and winnability/matrix runs.

contexts.name: CV Extraction & Pipeline Services
contexts.description: Parse and extract structure from CVs via Gemini, score soft signals, run the analysis pipeline orchestration and the long-running service, with redaction and i18n of prompts.

contexts.name: Matching Core (Taxonomy, Archetype & Transform)
contexts.description: The deterministic matching core: taxonomy definitions/graph, archetype resolution, candidate/job models, profile/profiling, skill transform/transferability and weight proposals.

contexts.name: LLM Benchmarking Harness (Python)
contexts.description: Offline benchmarking of provider/model quality: scenario definitions, an LLM-as-judge grader, the baking step that produces quality-score artifacts, and the bench CLI runner.

contexts.name: LLM Routing, Registry & Telemetry Core (Python)
contexts.description: The provider-agnostic routing core: the registry that picks an adapter by capability, capability declarations, config loading, an offline/fake mode for tests, monitoring/telemetry, and the CLI entrypoint for ad-hoc calls.

contexts.name: LLM Usage & Quality Reporting
contexts.description: Observability over LLM spend and output quality: the usage ledger, LightTrack integration, quality-score aggregation, and the Models tab's usage/quality overview panels.

contexts.name: API Key Store (Write-Only)
contexts.description: Secure, write-only storage of provider API keys: the DB store, secret-redaction/masking helpers so keys never round-trip to the client, and the Models tab's add-key form/list/panel.

contexts.name: Provider Routing Config & Preflight
contexts.description: Which LLM model/provider serves each capability: routing config storage, per-provider connectivity test, engine-availability preflight, Gemini retry policy, and the key-precedence resolver. Covers the Models tab's routing row/tab UI.

contexts.name: LLM Provider Adapters (Python)
contexts.description: Per-provider adapters implementing the common LLM base interface: Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Gemini and OpenRouter, plus the shared credentials loader and the base-interface test.

contexts.name: Org Benchmarks & Offer Analytics
contexts.description: External comparison analytics: role/archetype benchmark tables, org salary benchmarking, offer-leg and family-floor compensation panels, and automation-rate tracking, backed by the /api/benchmarks routes.

contexts.name: Channel Economics & Compute Cost
contexts.description: Cost-side analytics: channel spend input and economics panel, AI compute cost panel, sourcing-channel analytics, and the editable goals/target inputs (with the shared inline-number-save control) backed by the spend and targets API routes.

contexts.name: Decision Log & Records
contexts.description: The auditable log of hiring decisions: row/footer/toolbar composition for the live decision log plus the decision-records panel, its shared types, and the /api/analytics/decisions route that backs both.

contexts.name: Score Calibration & Thresholds
contexts.description: Calibrates AI screening scores against outcomes: reliability diagram, score bands, threshold history/suggestion strips and adverse-impact fairness checks, backed by the calibration lib and its API route. Governs how scoring thresholds evolve over time.

contexts.name: Forecast & Momentum Trends
contexts.description: Time-series analytics for the pipeline: hiring forecast, week-over-week momentum, delta chips and bottleneck detection, plus the drift strip surfacing them. Pure computation libs with their tests and the panels that render them; reads from the Analytics Shell context's data plumbing.

contexts.name: About & Feature Coverage
contexts.description: The About tab explaining how kp's features map onto the hiring pipeline, including the student-mode walkthrough (example scoring, interview script) and its supporting coverage/copy data. Split out of the former combined Matrix & Coverage context since it is a static explainer, not the interactive matrix.

contexts.name: Simulation Control Dock & On-Screen Surfaces
contexts.description: The visible chrome of the guided demo: the bottom SimBar and Control Dock (ops/sim faces, tiles), spotlight, explain drawer, decision wave, group-eval and offer frame overlays, plus the ControlRoom page and the diagram/style helpers they draw from. Consumes state from the Simulation Engine & Provider context rather than owning it.

contexts.name: Simulation Engine & Provider
contexts.description: The state engine behind the guided keyless JD→Hired demo: the sim-store, SimulationProvider/hooks driving phase walk and criteria, and the API routes that mutate demo state (apply-cv, inbound, offer-draft/link, reset, screen-draft). Owns the walk/phase sequencing and company templates that the on-screen surfaces render from.

contexts.name: Architecture Diagrams
contexts.description: The interactive pipeline/architecture diagrams page and the custom PlantUML-style Markdown renderer (elkjs layout) that draws component diagrams as styled SVG.

contexts.name: Skill Matrix
contexts.description: The candidate↔skill matrix view: grid, filter row, select bar, reasoning popover and toolbar over the matrix API, with the row/stat computation and tab-state hook behind it. Pure matrix presentation and interaction — the About/coverage explainer now lives in its own context.

contexts.name: Analytics Shell & Funnel Overview
contexts.description: The Analytics tab's overview shell: header, stat clusters, main grid and tab-chunk composition, plus the pipeline funnel panel and its empty-state guidance, backed by the core /api/analytics route and analytics DB access. Other analytics sub-contexts (forecast, calibration, decisions, spend, benchmarks) plug into this shell.

contexts.name: Billing Tab, Current Plan & Customer Portal
contexts.description: The Billing settings tab a signed-in user sees day to day: current-plan panel, usage meter row, status banners (past-due, canceled, etc.), and the customer-portal deep link/open flow.

contexts.name: Plan Catalog & Checkout
contexts.description: The plan catalog and checkout entry point: plan/price definitions, the checkout API that starts a Polar checkout session, and the catalog/price UI plus the setup script that provisions Polar products.

contexts.name: Billing Engine & Webhooks
contexts.description: Entitlement enforcement and the billing gateway (Polar): plan reduction, entitlement checks, webhook verification/sync. Gates premium capabilities across the app.

contexts.name: Shell E2E Test Suite
contexts.description: Playwright end-to-end specs exercising the app shell and top-level flows: analyze-smoke.spec.ts smoke-tests the analyze path, modal-escape.spec.ts verifies the Modal primitive's escape/focus-trap behavior at the app level, profile-builder.spec.ts covers the onboarding profile flow, and github-analysis.ts is the shared fixture data these specs import.

contexts.name: i18n & Localization
contexts.description: The next-intl localization layer: request.ts/server.ts/actions.ts wire locale detection and server-side translation lookup, locales.ts is the supported-locale registry, cs.json/en.json are the message catalogs, LanguageSwitcher.tsx is the user-facing toggle, and scripts/i18n-check.mjs is the CI contract that guards message-key parity between locales.

contexts.name: Route Error & Loading Boundaries (Token Routes)
contexts.description: The paired error.tsx/loading.tsx boundary files for every candidate/token-facing route segment (apply, data, devcase/apply, history, interview, jds, offer, onboarding, schedule, skill, status). These are thin Next.js convention files following the loading-choreography patterns in docs/LOADING_CHOREOGRAPHY.md; grouped together because they share the exact same skeleton/error-message pattern rather than any route-specific logic.

contexts.name: Root App Shell Scaffolding (Layout, Error & Not-Found Boundaries)
contexts.description: The app-root React tree that every route mounts inside: layout.tsx (html/body, providers, fonts), the top-level page.tsx dashboard entry, robots.ts/sitemap.ts for crawlers, and the root error.tsx/global-error.tsx/not-found.tsx boundaries plus login/loading.tsx. Distinct from the per-route error/loading boundaries below because these apply globally rather than to one candidate-facing token route.

contexts.name: Command Palette & Keyboard Shortcuts
contexts.description: The Cmd-K style command palette: WorkspaceCommandPalette/WorkspaceCommandPaletteList render it, useWorkspaceCommandPaletteItems builds the static+dynamic item catalog, useWorkspaceCommandPaletteSearch and workspacePaletteResults implement its fuzzy search against /api/search, and workspaceCommandPaletteTypes.ts is the shared shape. workspaceChords.ts and WorkspaceKeyboardShortcuts.tsx own the rest of the app's global keyboard-chord bindings (opening the palette, tab-switch chords, etc.), so they live alongside it.

contexts.name: Sidebar Nav Rail, Drawer & Recents
contexts.description: The just-refactored (see docs/FEATURE_STRUCTURE_REFACTOR.md) icon-rail-plus-panel navigation: NavSectionRail is the icon rail, NavPanelItem/NavRailBrandMark/NavRailPreferences render its panel content and footer, WorkspaceNav wires it to the active tab, and WorkspaceNavDrawer plus navDrawerA11y/navDrawerClose give it a focus-trapped mobile drawer variant. RecordRecent/WorkspaceRecentsNav/recents.ts track and surface the user's recently-visited items in that same rail.

contexts.name: System Health, Ops Telemetry & Dev Inspector
contexts.description: Operational plumbing that isn't user-facing: /api/health and /api/ops report liveness/ops telemetry (ops-telemetry.ts, scheduler-health.ts, site-url.ts, sales-contact.ts), python-runner.ts bridges to the Python scoring subprocess, and the DevInspector overlay (DevInspector.tsx, devInspectorUi.tsx, devLocate.ts) plus its build-time source-location injection scripts let a developer click a rendered element and jump to its source. instrumentation-node.ts and playwright.config.ts wire this tooling into the Next.js/test runtime.

contexts.name: Task Queue Backend & API
contexts.description: The server side of the background task system: tasks.ts is the persistence/enqueue/status API the rest of the app calls to register and poll async work, task-dedupe.ts prevents duplicate concurrent runs of the same logical task, and the /api/tasks routes (list, single, retry, history) expose that state to the Task Tracker UI and any external poller.

contexts.name: Score Visuals, Status Icons & Formatting Utilities
contexts.description: The result/report visual vocabulary reused across analysis, comparison and job-fit surfaces: Badge/PotentialBadge for status pills, ScoreBadge/ScoreDial/ScoreProvenanceLabel/Meter for numeric score display, and the small icon set (CompareIcon, ExtractionIcon, InterviewIcon, JobFitIcon, SalaryIcon) that labels those report sections. Bundled with the format.ts/initials.ts pure helpers (number/date formatting, name initials) that these visuals call to render their labels.

contexts.name: Form Primitives & Data-Fetching Hooks
contexts.description: The themed form-control family (Checkbox, Radio, Select, TextArea, TextInput, FileInput, RichTextEditor) plus the read-side rendering primitive Markdown/markdown-html.ts, and the generic client hooks that back form and list surfaces app-wide: useJsonFetch, useLoader, useInfiniteScroll, useReachOut, use-error-message, use-enum-label. Grouped together because most feature forms import both a control and one of these fetch/loading hooks in the same component.

contexts.name: Design Tokens, Theming & Brand Assets
contexts.description: The dual-theme (Studio Light / Spark Dark) foundation: globals.css defines every CSS variable token, useTheme.ts/theme.ts read and flip the `data-theme` attribute, ThemeToggle is the sidebar-footer switcher, and recipes.ts/SectionTitle.tsx are the composable surface/typography building blocks components pull from instead of re-typing Tailwind strings. Also owns the generated app icon/OG-image assets (apple-icon, opengraph-image, og-fonts) and the reduced-motion preference hook, since both key off the same theme/brand context.

contexts.name: URL, ID & Data Aggregation Utilities
contexts.description: Smaller pure-function helpers layered on top of the core infra utils: canonical public base-URL resolution, collision-safe random ID generation, comma-separated 'entries' query-param parsing, an array dedupe helper, a distribution/statistics helper (percentile-style math), and a generic array-splitting helper. Grouped separately from the core cache/env/rate-limit primitives because these are used more narrowly (query-string parsing, list math) rather than on every request.

contexts.name: Market Pulse Landing Visualization
contexts.description: The public Czech job-market data visualization embedded in the Spark landing experience: an interactive map (CzMap) and the MarketPulseApp/Atlas viewer that render pre-built market_pulse.json data (produced by the offline Market Pulse pumper pipeline) as charts and regional breakdowns. Also exposes a standalone /market route for direct/shared access outside the landing flow.

contexts.name: Branding & White-label
contexts.description: A white-label layer storing one org-level brand record (display name, hex accent color, https logo URL) in a lazily-created brand_settings table via the isolated-connection brand-store.ts, with validation centralized in the pure brand-config.ts (strict hex/URL sanitizers that make the injected accent CSS-injection-safe). The root layout reads getBrand() once and seeds BrandProvider (fetch-free context for BrandHeader) and BrandStyle (a server-rendered <style> overriding the --color-coral design token app-wide, including candidate-facing pages). BrandingTab reads/writes /api/brand and applies the accent live on save.

contexts.name: Landing & Marketing
contexts.description: The public, logged-out marketing surface: the Studio 'about' page, the Spark-art-direction home/landing pages (hero, feature previews, pricing section, language switch for anonymous visitors), and the login entry page. These pages own no app data and read no auth session; they are pure presentation plus the Spark tokens/illustrations that skin them.

contexts.name: Shared Utility Libraries
contexts.description: Cross-cutting request/response and infra utilities used app-wide: a uniform API-response shaper, an in-memory cache with typed keys, structured logging, env-var parsing/validation, sliding-window rate limiting, request-body helpers, and URL-safety sanitizers. These are the primitives every route handler and server action leans on before touching business logic.

contexts.name: Behavioral UI Primitives (Modal, Toast, Loading & Errors)
contexts.description: The interaction-state primitives shared by every feature surface: Modal (with focus-trap via useDialogA11y), the Toast notification stack and its store, SegmentedControl and its shared-layout selection logic, and the loading/error/empty-state family (Skeleton, LoadStatus, RouteError, RouteLoading, ErrorBoundary, ChainEmptyState, CompletionCta). These render identically in both Studio Light and Spark Dark by resolving through CSS tokens, not hardcoded color.

contexts.name: Background Task Tracker UI
contexts.description: The Tasks tab surface end users see: TasksProvider streams task state to TasksIndicator (header badge) and TasksTab (full list), TasksGroup/TasksDoneRow/TasksFilterBar/TasksResultsSection render the active/history breakdown, and TasksActiveCard/TasksBackupCard/TasksSystemCard/TasksBackupRestorePlan render per-task-kind detail cards (including the backup-restore plan preview). tasksTabHelpers.ts, tasksTaskMeter.ts and useTaskResult.ts are the view-model glue between the provider and these cards.

contexts.name: Workspace Tab Catalog, Attention & Live Refresh
contexts.description: The authenticated Workspace root (Workspace.tsx) that mounts the active tab from the tab catalog (tabs.ts), lazily chunks tab bundles (WorkspaceTabChunks.tsx) and renders the guided-simulation overlay (WorkspaceSimSurfaces.tsx). live-refresh.ts polls for backend changes while a tab is open; attention.ts/useAttention.ts compute the per-tab 'needs attention' badge counts surfaced in the nav rail; /control is the dev-only simulation control page.

contexts.name: Workspace Export, Import & Portability
contexts.description: Data-portability layer for a workspace: full export/import of a workspace's data, the workspace lock used during import, load-state bootstrapping, and the DB path/portability helpers plus the CLI scripts that dump/load a DB file.

contexts.name: Tenancy Scoping, Guards & Workspace Switching
contexts.description: Request-time tenancy enforcement: edge-runtime token verification in the proxy, the current-workspace resolver, home-gate redirect logic, operator-only route guards, and the switch-workspace API that flips a session's active tenant.

contexts.name: Salary & Org Benchmark Data
contexts.description: DB stores for compensation/organization benchmarking: salary benchmark tables and the seed script that populates a sample benchmark team, used by comp-analysis features elsewhere in the app.

contexts.name: First-Run Setup & Onboarding Wizard
contexts.description: The first-run onboarding wizard shown to a brand-new organization: company/name capture, first-role draft, invite teammates step, and the getting-started checklist/handoff summary shown after setup completes. Purely a guided UI flow over the org/invite/job libraries owned elsewhere.

contexts.name: Member Roster, Roles & Permissions
contexts.description: The recruiter-facing member roster: listing/removing members, editing per-member capability overrides, and the five-role capability model that resolves permissions live per request. Covers the Organization tab's member panel/table/modals plus the roles/operator-approval library backing them.

contexts.name: Organization Core, Settings & Invites
contexts.description: The organization aggregate root and its invite lifecycle: org creation/settings persistence, the org-service business-rule layer (last-owner protection, capability resolution hooks), tenancy helpers, and the tokenized invite flow that mints a user + membership and auto-signs the invitee in. This is the entry point other org sub-contexts (member roster, setup wizard) call into.

contexts.name: Privacy, Consent & Provenance
contexts.description: GDPR-oriented consent capture and gating, AI-usage disclosure to candidates, and the provenance dossier that records how each data point was derived.

contexts.name: Data Store & Persistence Core
contexts.description: The SQLite persistence foundation shared by every feature store: the core DB handle/connection, generated and hand-written schemas, the null contract, Postgres-portability shim, and DB path/portability helpers.

contexts.name: Login & Session Issuing
contexts.description: Password verification and session issuing: login/logout API routes, the login page client, session cookie creation/read helpers, and the dev-only e2e auth bypass used by end-to-end tests.
